content:
**#518: un tercio de main sin auditar**

A third of main was never audited, and the design question that held the fix made the model SIMPLER.

The walk selected `git log --first-parent --merges`. `--merges` means more than one parent, so a squash was never enumerated — not evaluated and passed: never looked at. Measured on origin/main over 60 days: 112 first-parent commits, 79 enumerated, 33 never audited (32 carrying a (#N) reference).

It compounded: a window with no findings exits 0, the cursor advances, and since the cursor only moves forward every unenumerated commit became PERMANENTLY un-re-auditable. No remediation path either — [FAIL-SHA] can only nominate a commit the audit enumerated.

The held question: every exemption predicate is built on `<sha>^1..<sha>` and nothing had decided what that means with no second parent. Answer: `^1` resolves for ANY non-root commit, and for a linear one it is simply its own diff — less ambiguous than a merge's contribution. So sign/netPresent/netAddFull/addedPathsAbsentAt needed NO change. Only the three ENUMERATORS moved, and together — widening one alone leaves the two sides disagreeing about what a window contains, worse than either narrow one.

Consequence: every commit on the integration line is now governed, including direct pushes. --first-parent untouched. Existing history is not re-audited.
